what_is_ssy.title: What is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)?
what_is_ssy.body: The Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a government-backed savings scheme launched as part of the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' campaign. It's designed to encourage parents to build a fund for their female child's future education and marriage expenses.

quick_facts.title: Quick Facts:
points: High Interest Rate: Currently offers one of the highest interest rates among small savings schemes.
Tax Benefits: Enjoys Exempt-Exempt-Exempt (EEE) status, similar to PPF.
Eligibility: For a girl child below the age of 10.

investment_strategy.title: How to Maximize SSY Returns
points: Invest Early: Start as soon as your daughter is born to maximize the compounding period.
Invest Before 5th of April: To get interest for the full financial year, make your lump-sum deposit before April 5th.
Maximize Contribution: If possible, contribute the maximum ₹1.5 lakh annually to build a substantial corpus.
investment_strategy.monthly_example: If investing monthly, ensure your SIP is debited before the 5th of each month to be eligible for that month's interest calculation.

tax_benefits.title: Tax Benefits of SSY
tax_benefits.intro: SSY is a powerful tax-saving tool with an EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) status:
tax_benefits.body: This means the contribution (up to ₹1.5 lakh under 80C), the interest earned, and the maturity amount are all completely tax-free.

rules.title: Key Rules of SSY
rules.withdrawal_body: Partial withdrawal of up to 50% of the balance is allowed for the girl's higher education once she turns 18. Full withdrawal is allowed upon maturity at 21 years, or at the time of her marriage after she turns 18.
rules.withdrawal_example: For example, if the balance is ₹40 lakh when your daughter turns 18, you can withdraw up to ₹20 lakh for her college fees.
rules.revival_intro: If the minimum annual deposit of ₹250 is not made, the account becomes discontinued. It can be revived by paying:
revival_steps: A penalty of ₹50 for each year of default.
The minimum subscription amount (₹250) for each default year.
rules.nomination_body: Nomination facility is not available in an SSY account, as the account is in the name of the girl child who is the beneficiary.

how_to_open.title: How to Open an SSY Account
how_to_open.intro: You can open an SSY account at any authorized bank or post office. The process involves:
steps: Filling the SSY account opening form.
Submitting the girl child's birth certificate.
Submitting KYC documents of the parent/guardian (ID and address proof).
Making the first deposit (from ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh).

faqs.question: Can I open two SSY accounts for one daughter?
faqs.answer: No, only one SSY account is allowed per girl child.

faqs.question: Can a family open three SSY accounts if they have three daughters?
faqs.answer: A family can open a maximum of two SSY accounts. A third account is only permissible in the case of twin or triplet girls born after the first child.

faqs.question: What is the minimum and maximum amount I can deposit in an SSY account?
faqs.answer: The minimum annual deposit is ₹250, and the maximum is ₹1,50,000 in a financial year.

faqs.question: When does the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account mature?
faqs.answer: The account matures 21 years from the date of account opening, or at the time of the girl's marriage after she attains the age of 18.

conclusion.title: A Powerful Tool for Your Daughter's Future
conclusion.body: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is more than just a savings scheme; it's a commitment to your daughter's bright future. With its high, tax-free returns and government backing, it is one of the best tools available for planning her education and marriage expenses. Use this calculator to visualize the growth and take a confident step towards securing her dreams.
